solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put an end to distilled drink

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to stop it dead

explanation.surface: Someone calls time on the drinking of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: the verb is to quash or stamp out, the noun is malt whisky from Scotland.

clue.text: Sinister look is arising in case of cowboy

indicators.note: in means the reversed look word goes inside the cowboy's outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only the first and last letters of cowboy are used
in a down clue, rising means the word for look is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A menacing glance appears on a cowboy's face in a western.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinister gives you the shivers, which is exactly the eerie, unsettling sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Team Dane assembled adopts right commercial tag?

indicators.note: adopts means the shuffled letters take the abbreviation into their midst
assembled means the letters of team and Dane are put together in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Danish team gets together and picks a brand name for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges TEAMDANE into TADENAME, and 'adopts' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand label attached to a product for sale, protected so rivals cannot use it, is a commercial tag.

clue.text: Ace in Indianopolis if in charge gets respectful title

parts.note: in card games an ace is an honour card, and in American spelling (as in Indianapolis) the word drops its u

explanation.surface: An outstanding performer in Indianapolis, if put in charge, earns a mark of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace, king, queen, jack and ten are the honours in bridge; 'in Indianopolis' asks for the US spelling without U.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorific is a form of address such as Sir or Dame that conveys esteem.

clue.text: Passage in port, say, entered by Dee and Philip

indicators.note: entered by means the drink has the letter and the nickname go inside it

parts.note: port is an example of a fortified wine
Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
Pip is a short form of Philip, as in Great Expectations

explanation.surface: A route through a harbour taken by two people called Dee and Philip.
explanation.walkthrough: Dee looks like the river, but here it just spells out the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the air passage running from the throat down to the lungs.

clue.text: Belligerent type from west arrived with French king after revolution

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the French word for king is read backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A fighter came in from the west with a French monarch after a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Revolution in the surface is a red herring: 'after revolution' only turns the king word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior is a fighter, someone who is aggressive or eager for combat.

clue.text: Relative emitting relieved expression with friend in the country

indicators.note: emitting means letting out, so the exclamation comes out of the relative

parts.note: a nephew is a family relative
phew is what you say when relieved
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A family member breathes a sigh of relief while in the country with a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitting' takes PHEW out of NEPHEW, which leaves NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Student tucks into French bread of an ordinary type

indicators.note: tucks into means the student letter is placed inside the French word

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread
L is the learner plate, a common shorthand for student

explanation.surface: A student eats a simple French loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating but places L inside PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple or unadorned, not fancy, which is what an ordinary sort of thing is.

clue.text: Chap's tie is crooked jumble

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's necktie is askew and messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the letters of CHAPSTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche can mean a hotchpotch or medley of styles and pieces, which is a jumble.

clue.text: Fantastic trainee beginning to recoup fee

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters of trainee are reworked
beginning to means only the opening letter of recoup is used

explanation.surface: A brilliant apprentice starts to earn back what was paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges TRAINEE into RETAINE, and R is the first letter of recoup.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an advance payment made to secure a lawyer's or adviser's services.

clue.text: Artist is engaged in exercise to get approval

indicators.note: is engaged in means the artist and the word is sit inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A painter takes up physical training and wins applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is the expression of admiration or approval for someone.

clue.text: Look in a place for summer entertainment, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken and heard as a different word

parts.note: a seaside pier, with its amusements and end-of-pier shows, is a place for summer fun

explanation.surface: Someone checks out a holiday venue for summer shows.
explanation.walkthrough: British seaside piers traditionally host summer variety shows and arcades.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to seem, as in 'he looks tired', so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Trouble one found with much of report in US state

parts.note: ill as a noun is harm or trouble
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: much of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a report can be a loud bang, a noise

explanation.surface: Bad news turns up in a report from an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' cuts NOISE to NOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty states, home to Chicago.

clue.text: Doubts in fast regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words in and fast

explanation.surface: Uncertainties are on show during a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs as a noun are conditions or uncertainties, as in 'no ifs or buts'.

clue.text: Artist's fight is misjudged when initially viewed?

indicators.note: misjudged means wrongly assessed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter's brawl is wrongly assessed by those who see it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misjudged' shuffles ARTISTSFIGHT; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a first glance or first impression, as in love on first seeing someone.

clue.text: First-class cartoonist with a global reputation?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for the highest quality or social rank
read literally, someone who draws and is at the top of the world

explanation.surface: An outstanding cartoonist famous everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means of the best quality; split, it is a drawer who is at the top.

clue.text: Irish woman starts to become loud and extremely easily annoyed

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: An Irish woman begins to get noisy and very touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' picks B, L and E from become, loud and extremely. 'extremely easily' looks like a pair, but 'easily' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritable person is quick to anger or short-tempered.

clue.text: Persist taking right-wing money upsetting Eurosceptics' enemy?

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the right-wing party
tin is an old slang word for money

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting means turning upside down, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Eurosceptics oppose the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: A Tory keeps going, taking cash and annoying the opponents of Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses EU to UE. The question mark flags that the EU is described by who dislikes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to carry on or keep going, which is what it means to persist.

clue.text: Unusually poor rep came round clubs to suffer a fall

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the clubs abbreviation
unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the anagram fodder
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A man with a bad name took a tumble despite carrying golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges POORREPCAME and 'round' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fall heavily, originally from horse riding, or figuratively to fail badly.

clue.text: Measure of current in uncovered light source

indicators.note: uncovered means the top, which in a down clue is the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a lamp is a source of light

explanation.surface: Electrical current is measured in an exposed lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' removes the first letter of LAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for ampere, the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Complete challenge between two people largely late in the day?

parts.note: over means finished, complete

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two people

explanation.surface: A finished two-person contest ending late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims DUEL to DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past the expected time, so the playful definition of being late, not just at a late hour, fits.

clue.text: Pairs of deeply jaded vulgarians offering tired stuff

indicators.note: pairs of means the first two letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: Very jaded boors serving up stale material.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for 'already seen' also describes something stale and overfamiliar.

clue.text: Special front of a document, maybe, showing obstacle?

parts.note: the first sheet of a document is its top page

explanation.surface: A special cover sheet appears to be a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a blockage or halt, something that holds things up.

clue.text: Solid priest is overseeing mass

indicators.note: in a down clue, overseeing means sitting above, so the mass letter comes below

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A reliable cleric supervises the celebration of Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective describing the priest; it is a noun, the geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a three-dimensional geometric figure, so it is a solid in maths.

clue.text: Stadium put up in Brisbane rapidly

indicators.note: put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sports ground is erected quickly in Brisbane.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, a stadium.

clue.text: Terrible tenor off-key around end of concert

indicators.note: around means the rearranged singer goes around that letter
off-key means out of tune, so the letters of tenor are reworked

parts.note: the five letters of the singer's voice are the anagram fodder

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of concert is used

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A dreadful tenor sings out of tune near the end of the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-key' makes ROTEN from TENOR, 'around' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten in its informal sense means awful or very poor.

clue.text: Provoke citizen in middle of diner

indicators.note: in means the short citizen word goes inside those middle letters
middle of means the letters of diner without its two ends

parts.note: its central three letters are used, without the two ends
cit is an old short form of citizen

explanation.surface: A troublemaker stirs up a resident in the middle of a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or urge on, to provoke someone into acting.

clue.text: Gloomy director gets to admit defeat

parts.note: to own up is to admit, and own alone can mean confess
to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: A miserable film boss concedes that he lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit defeat' reads as one idiom, but each word does its own job.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat means pessimistic or depressed, the same mood as gloomy.

clue.text: Go through Russian city with European friend short of money

parts.note: Perm is a city in the Ural region of Russia

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the money letter is taken out of the friend word

parts.note: mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A trip round a Russian city with a European pal who is out of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' takes M from MATE, leaving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through or seep into every part, to penetrate.

clue.text: Melancholy skipper with no more appetite, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, skips along, and one with no more appetite is full

explanation.surface: A sad ship's captain has lost his appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' wants to be a captain; it is a kangaroo (roo), which skips about.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means expressing regret in a sorrowful way, so it is close to sad or mournful.
